justification_text:
The consistent point estimate of 14.93 across the one-day, one-week, and one-month horizons was primarily driven by the observed stability of the underlying metric at the time the forecast was made. This suggests that the current value, or a very recent average, served as the most robust baseline for our expectations. There were no immediate indicators, anticipated events, or discernible trends that would predictably cause a significant directional shift in the short to medium term, leading to an expectation that the prevailing conditions would largely continue to hold steady.

The widening of the 90% confidence intervals as the forecast horizon extended directly reflects the escalating uncertainty inherent in projecting future outcomes over time. For the one-day forecast, the tight interval of [14.63, 15.23] indicates high confidence in minimal short-term deviation, likely influenced by the inertia of the system or market. As we moved to one week ([14.33, 15.53]) and especially to one month ([13.66, 16.2]), the range broadened significantly. This expansion accounts for an increasing number of potential factors that could influence the metric, such as the accumulation of minor fluctuations, the release of new economic data, shifts in market sentiment, or subtle changes in underlying conditions that become more pronounced over longer periods. Essentially, the further into the future one looks, the more variables can come into play and compound their effects, making precise prediction more challenging.

While these intervals capture a significant portion of expected variability, certain high-impact, unforeseen events could push outcomes beyond the stated boundaries. These might include sudden and drastic shifts in global economic conditions, such as a major recession or an unexpected boom, significant geopolitical developments that disrupt prevailing stability, or abrupt changes in regulatory policies pertinent to the metric being forecasted. Additionally, major technological breakthroughs or unforeseen disruptions could fundamentally alter the environment, creating outcomes that lie outside the probabilistic distributions considered when formulating these intervals.
